feedback.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,0,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨4,0,2⟩=16.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨4,0,2⟩=16$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨4,0,2⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨4,0,2⟩ & =0 \\ 4{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3} & =0 \\ 2{t}_{3} & =-4{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{3} & =-2{t}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,{t}_{2},\,-2{t}_{1}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{2}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the second component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{2}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{1}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{1}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{c}=-\frac{1}{2}.$
